scenes.heading: Finding sides and angles
scenes.sub: One side and one angle tell you everything
scenes.say: You can’t always reach the side you want to measure. But if you know one side and one angle of a right-angled triangle, trigonometry gives you the rest.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Dollars to yen: multiply. Yen to dollars: divide.
scenes.science: x on top of the ratio: multiply. x on the bottom: divide.
scenes.breaks: Exchange rates change every day. sin 40° never changes.
scenes.say: Think of a currency converter. To change dollars into yen you multiply by the rate. To change back, you divide. A trig ratio is an exchange rate between two sides. If x is on top of the fraction, multiply. If x is on the bottom, divide.

scenes.heading: Four steps
steps: Label H, O, A from the angle
scenes.say: Every problem uses the same four steps. Label the sides from the angle. Choose the ratio that uses the side you know and the side you want. Write the equation. Then solve it, and round only at the very end.

scenes.heading: x on top: multiply
scenes.say: Here is a triangle with a forty degree angle and a hypotenuse of fifteen centimetres. Now we mark x, opposite the angle. Opposite and hypotenuse means sine. Sine forty equals x over fifteen, so x equals fifteen times sine forty, about nine point six centimetres.
scenes.caption: sin 40° = x/15, so x = 15 sin 40° ≈ 9.6 cm.

scenes.heading: x on the bottom: divide
scenes.question: Angle 28°, opposite side 6 m. Find the hypotenuse x.
scenes.say: Now the opposite side is six metres and we want the hypotenuse. Sine twenty-eight equals six over x. This time x is on the bottom, so divide: six divided by sine twenty-eight is about twelve point eight metres. It’s longer than six, so it makes sense.

scenes.heading: Finding an angle
scenes.question: Adjacent side 7 cm, hypotenuse 11 cm. Find θ.
scenes.say: To find an angle, write the ratio as a fraction, then use the inverse key. Cos theta equals seven over eleven, so theta equals inverse cos of seven elevenths, about fifty point five degrees.

scenes.heading: Two triangles: shared side first
scenes.say: Some diagrams hide two right-angled triangles. First draw triangle A B C, then the dashed height A D. Find the shared side first: A D is twelve times sine fifty. Then A C is A D divided by sine thirty-five, about sixteen centimetres. Keep A D unrounded in between.
scenes.caption: AD = 12 sin 50° ≈ 9.19. Then AC = AD ÷ sin 35° ≈ 16.0 cm.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Label, choose, write, solve. If x is on top, multiply. If x is on the bottom, divide. To find an angle, use the inverse keys. And with two triangles, find the shared side first. Now try the practice questions!
